assertions.text: Output contains a markdown table (using | column | syntax)
assertions.evidence: | Scenario | Applicant Age | Credit Score | Income Status | Min Score (Policy) | Approved? | Rejection Reason? |

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?'
assertions.evidence: "Approved?" and "Rejection Reason?" are output column headers that end with '?'

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language — no implementation terms
assertions.evidence: Column headers: 'Scenario', 'Applicant Age', 'Credit Score', 'Income Status', 'Min Score (Policy)', 'Approved?', 'Rejection Reason?' — all use business domain language, no camelCase terms like 'creditScore' or 'isEligible'

assertions.text: Table includes at least one row specifically for the senior applicant (65+) threshold scenario
assertions.evidence: Multiple senior threshold rows present: 'Just at senior age | 65 | 620 | stable | 600 | yes' and 'Senior, at senior threshold — not above | 70 | 600 | stable | 600 | no'

assertions.text: The missing income scenario is represented with open/uncertain expected value and/or explicit open question note
assertions.evidence: 'Standard adult, income not provided' and 'Senior, income not provided' rows both show **?** in the Approved? column with 'Open: reject (missing = unstable) or block (require info)?' note

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions not outcomes
assertions.evidence: All scenario names describe conditions: 'Standard adult, at threshold — not above', 'Senior, score meets senior threshold', 'Senior, unstable income' — none are named after outcomes like 'Approved' or 'Rejected'

assertions.text: Policy thresholds (650 for standard, 600 for senior) appear as concrete values in Credit Score column
assertions.evidence: Credit Score column contains boundary values: 650 appears in 'Standard adult, at threshold — not above' row and 600 appears in 'Senior, at senior threshold — not above' row
